speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you've described a concerning set of symptoms: fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These are often referred to as "B symptoms" in lymphoma, but I need to narrow this down. Have you noticed any recent infections, fevers, or skin rashes?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, LDH_level.

speaker: Measurement
text:
RESULTS: 
Complete Blood Count with Differential: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal
Comprehensive Metabolic Panel: Normal Readings (not provided in source data)
LDH Level: Elevated

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for sharing that history; the combination of smoking, weight loss, night sweats, and specifically enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes raises concern for malignancy despite the previous tuberculosis diagnosis. To differentiate between an infectious etiology and a potential lymphoma, I need to see your recent blood work and evaluate your lymph nodes directly. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count_with_Differential, Comprehensive_Metabolic_Panel, LDH_level. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Lymph_Node_Ultrasound.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: COMPLETE BLOOD COUNT WITH DIFFERENTIAL: WBC Elevated, Hemoglobin Slightly Decreased, Platelets Normal; COMPREHENSIVE METABOLIC PANEL: NORMAL READINGS; LDH LEVEL: Elevated; CERVICAL LYMPH NODE ULTRASOUND: Not provided in source data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated LDH and abnormal blood counts alongside your smoking history and "B symptoms" strongly suggest a malignancy rather than tuberculosis. Since the lymph node ultrasound wasn't returned, I need to see the internal structure and tissue sample to confirm. Please undergo an excisional biopsy of the enlarged supraclavicular node. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_CT_scan. REQUEST TEST: Excisional_Lymph_Node_Biopsy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CT Scan Thorax and Abdomen: Findings - Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Excisional Lymph Node Biopsy: Findings - Lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma (DLBCL). The biopsy showing CD20-positive lymphocytes with a high proliferative index, combined with the massive lymphadenopathy on CT and B symptoms, confirms this aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma. We will proceed immediately to staging and chemotherapy planning.
